stem: Sodium oxide, $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, is a white crystalline solid with a high melting point.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of sodium with oxygen, forming sodium oxide. Include state symbols.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why sodium oxide has a high melting point.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: When sodium oxide reacts with water an alkaline solution is obtained.
parts.text: Explain why the solution obtained is alkaline. You should use the Brønsted-Lowry theory of acids and bases in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the pH of the solution obtained when $3.10\text{ g}$ of sodium oxide are added to $400\text{ cm}^3$ of water.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Use the data below, and other suitable data from the *Data Booklet*, to calculate the lattice energy of sodium oxide, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{latt}} \text{Na}_2\text{O(s)}$.

| standard enthalpy change of formation of sodium oxide, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{f}} \text{Na}_2\text{O(s)}$ | -416 |
| standard enthalpy change of atomisation of sodium, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{at}} \text{Na(s)}$ | +109 |
| electron affinity of $\text{O(g)}$ | -142 |
